To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) commodity exporting countries may achieve higher welfare under a revenue-maximizing export tax than under a welfare-maximizing export tariff; (2) the welfare maximizing tariff is always greater than the revenue maximizing export tariff; and (3) a commodity exporting country may achieve higher welfare with a tariff rate that is greater than its welfare maximizing tariff rate.

commodity exporting countries can obtain higher welfare under revenue-maximizing export taxes than under the traditional welfare maximizing export taxes, and this result is not obtained in the standard two-country models.
the welfare maximizing export tax rate is not the same as the revenue maximizing export tax rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Can revenue maximizing export taxes (REXT) yield higher welfare than the welfare maximizing export taxes (WEXT) for commodity exporting countries?
the following question: can the revenue maximizing export tax yield higher welfare than the welfare maximizing export tax in a three country world?
the following questions: 1) What is the optimal tax structure of the export commodity?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
revenue maximizing export taxes can lead to higher welfare than welfare-maximizing export taxes in commodity exporting countries.
, under certain conditions, revenue maximizing export taxes are welfare improving.

the welfare maximizing export tax is the best tax policy in the sense that the welfare of the country is higher than that obtained under revenue maximizing export tax, and that the revenue maximizing export tax is better than the revenue maximizing import tax.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the welfare maximizing tax rule is only a necessary condition for welfare maximization.
the traditional models are not sufficient to explain the actual export tax policy of commodity exporting countries.
the traditional welfare maximization criterion may not be the appropriate one for the developing countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the welfare maximizing export taxes may be too high to be implemented by the commodity exporting countries.
the welfare maximizing export tax may not be the best policy for a commodity exporting country to follow.
revenue maximizing export taxes can be welfare maximizing export taxes in a three-country model with two commodities and a third country which is a net importer.
